title: "Files, releases and versions"
description: "Identify authoritative, private, public and mirrored BNR files and apply current version rules."

## Location determines authority

| Location type | Contents | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Authoritative source | REDCap or another approved controlled source | Correct records here, never in an extract. |
| Private working storage | extracts, confidential and deidentified inputs, candidates, logs, QA and review evidence | Keep outside Git and limit to authorised users. |
| Authoritative public storage | approved published metric and report packages | Publication controllers write and verify these packages. |
| Website mirror | approved public datasets, reports and metadata consumed by Quarto | Replaceable from the authoritative public package. |
| Git repository | code, Quarto source and public-safe static assets | Never store confidential or private control material. |

## Release identity

Use the complete workflow identity—product, reporting period, source release and
version—at every step. Do not rely on a filename containing `current` to
identify the source of a reproducible build.

Event and mortality workflows create release-stamped public packages and a
controlled current mirror where required. The rolling update freezes complete
copies of its exact event and mortality source CSVs inside the dated report
package.

## Report version rules

- Rolling updates use a positive version. Replacing an existing period requires
  an explicitly authorised, strictly higher version.
- Annual reports use an identity such as
  `bnr_cvd_annual_report_2025_v1`; corrections use a higher version while the
  public period location remains stable.
- One-off reports use a controlled report ID and positive version; a changed
  approved PDF requires a new candidate and version.
- Never reuse a version number for different content.

## Approval binding

An approval applies only to the exact candidate identified by its manifest,
fingerprint or equivalent workflow controls. Publication must read the
controlled approved payload. If any payload file changes, rebuild and obtain a
new approval.

## Corrections and recovery

| Problem | Action |
|---|---|
| Source record wrong | Correct the authoritative source and rerun from extraction. |
| Calculation or suppression wrong | Correct version-controlled Stata code and rerun. |
| Report result wrong | Correct its source or analytical code, rebuild and issue the required higher version. |
| Quarto wording or layout wrong | Correct Quarto source; repeat substantive review if interpretation changes. |
| Website mirror missing or damaged | Recreate it from the authoritative approved package. |

Do not retain duplicate “new” pages or manually patched generated files.
Use Git history to recover version-controlled source and the controlled
authoritative stores to recover approved public packages.

## Before deployment

Check that Git status contains only intended public-safe source and approved
public assets. Private paths, tokens, logs, approval evidence, workbooks and
staging files must not be committed.
